sourceInformation.source: Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (1982 video game), inspired by the film’s snow battle
sourceInformation.perspective: Third-person elevated chase, optional tactical overhead camera
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPURenderer (WebGPU; WebGL 2 fallback), Rapier 0.19.3, Gamepad API, Web Audio API, WebRTC, BroadcastChannel, AI Hub Session Protocol v1 client 1.4.0; bundled with esbuild 0.25.12
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural stylized cel shading, ink silhouettes, faceted glacier scenery and printed-comic interface
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer, AnimationClip and keyframe tracks; custom walker gait, topple, engine pulse, raider idle and repair-beacon animations
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-written oscillator music, synthesized effects and Animalese-style gibberish radio voices; no audio files. Music defaults to 10%.
sourceInformation.online: 1–4 AI Hub ghost-rival sessions; standalone same-origin BroadcastChannel wing echoes and two-player serverless WebRTC pairing with manual signaling. Direct WebRTC requires a reachable network.
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium 153; WebGPU and WebGL 2; scripted complete mission and attract replay, emulated standard gamepad, simultaneous touch at 844×390, portrait-phone layout at 390×844, iPad device profile, live/offline audio signals, two-page BroadcastChannel and WebRTC, and the official AI Hub harness with 2/4 players, 150 ms latency, 50 ms jitter, 5% loss and host departure. Physical-device/listening review unknown.
sourceInformation.research: No internet search or source research. Native model knowledge; downloaded the explicitly requested AI Hub integration contract/client/harness and pinned runtime dependencies.

testingFeedback: Testing caught 8 issues: inline-script packaging corruption, reversed craft face winding, Enter launching after leaving attract mode, twin cannon rays missing the aim point, stale victory state on restart, a tow camera that cropped the walker, edge markers overlapping the hull display, and keyboard hints appearing on the touch title screen. All were fixed. The final suite has 71 passing checks.
2 critical issues: the initial startup packaging error and unreliable cannon convergence. Both were fixed.
The complete AI playthrough and independent attract-mode playthrough: they exercise real Rapier projectile hits, both cable takedowns, escort progression, the ace, victory, and the replay loop.
Headless WebGPU screenshots were blank on this machine. State checks verified WebGPU, and WebGL screenshots supplied the visual review.
engineFeedback: Three.js makes procedural geometry, banded toon shading, native transform animation and multiple camera styles straightforward. WebGPURenderer also supplies a useful WebGL 2 backend.
I initially reversed the custom wedge mesh winding and aimed parallel twin-gun rays beside the target. Visual review and actual Rapier hit tests exposed these assumptions; both were corrected.
The arcade flight model, guided tow orbit and tension mechanic, data-driven mission, controller menu focus, synthesized audio and ghost-rival transports.
Coordinating WebGPU initialization and headless visual capture while keeping physics, animation, input and multiplayer lifecycles consistent.
A documented, reliable headless screenshot path across WebGPU adapters and fallback backends.
promptFeedback: The specific source, cel-shaded direction, controller-first UX, attract mode and complete-demo requirements provided a clear identity and useful acceptance criteria.
The source title also names the film, while 1982 identifies the original video game. I used the snow-battle arcade game as the mechanical anchor and the film for tone.
Making cable takedowns readable and satisfying across controller, mouse and simultaneous touch while delivering all mission stages and multiplayer paths.
Specify whether standalone multiplayer must cross NAT without manual signaling, and whether a WebGL fallback is desired.

aiHub.name: The Empire Strikes a Pose
aiHub.tagline: Big feet. Small problem. Very long cable.
aiHub.description: Skim an ink-drawn ice valley, clear enemy scouts and wrap the legs of walking fortresses. Escort thirty-eight refugees through a final ace attack, with wing echoes for score-chasing friends.
aiHub.source: Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (1982)
aiHub.controls: WASD steer/throttle, mouse aim/fire, Shift boost, Space tow, Q lock, C camera, Esc pause; standard pad LS/R2/L2/Cross; assisted dual-drag touch.
